conventions: Format all TypeScript, TSX, JSON, and Markdown files with Prettier (2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas) and lint TS/TSX with ESLint.

Group imports with blank lines between external packages, @excalidraw/* workspace value imports, @excalidraw/* type-only imports, relative value imports, and relative type-only imports; use `import type` for type-only imports.
Omit `arrowheadSize` on newly created or restored linear elements when `arrowheadSize === undefined` so default element shapes and existing snapshots are unchanged.
Use Vitest (`describe`, `it`, `expect`) and `@testing-library/react` (`fireEvent`, `queryByTestId`) with `API` test helpers for unit and component tests.
Add English UI strings only to `packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json`; never edit other locale files.

decisions.topic: Arrowhead size multiplier representation and preset values
decisions.choice: Optional `arrowheadSize?: number` on `ExcalidrawLinearElement` defaulting to `1` when omitted, with UI presets Small = `0.5`, Medium = `1`, Large = `1.5`
decisions.reason: A numeric multiplier supports arbitrary positive finite values in scene JSON and skeleton API while keeping presets simple and avoiding off-limits AppState changes.

decisions.topic: Arrowhead size radio option testIds and i18n label key
decisions.choice: Use `data-testid` values `"arrowhead-size-small"`, `"arrowhead-size-medium"`, and `"arrowhead-size-large"` with group `"arrowhead-size"` and label key `"labels.arrowheadSize"`
decisions.reason: Matches FR-12 and provides deterministic selectors for properties panel tests.

decisions.topic: Clearing arrowheadSize on undo/redo and style paste
decisions.choice: When applying a delta or pasting styles with `arrowheadSize: undefined`, pass `force = true` to `newElementWith` and `delete` the `arrowheadSize` property from the resulting element
rejected: Calling `newElementWith(el, { arrowheadSize: undefined })` without `force` or leaving `arrowheadSize: undefined` as an own property
decisions.reason: `newElementWith` ignores `undefined` values unless `force = true`, and deleting the key restores the omitted-property state.
